judge_notes: Correct COIN/HOOD weights but says an unidentified issuer in a distinct residual totaling only 30% might breach the >50% rule; therefore wrongly withholds the portfolio-wide no-breach conclusion.
Says only the two named issuers can be cleared and the portfolio policy cannot be evaluated, although every other distinct issuer is bounded by the entire 30% residual.
Finally derives the correct no-breach bound and states it in the bottom line, but first calls the residual issuer question unresolvable; contradictory wording keeps it below high.
Correct known weights but claims an unknown issuer in a 30%-of-total residual might breach the 50%-of-total limit; its additional residual-percentage arithmetic is inconsistent.
Correctly clears COIN and HOOD but insists the portfolio-wide >50% rule remains indeterminate despite the distinct residual's 30% total cap.
Correct issuer-aggregation ranges COIN 40-70 and HOOD 30-60, conditional strict threshold and unresolved verdict; SEC evidence is two-sided and does not become factor exposure.
Correct unresolved policy and conditional sleeve thresholds; calls the COIN prior-year comparison a weak base without a selected-packet history benchmark.
Correctly identifies issuer overlap and missing aggregate, but says an entirely new issuer in a 30% sleeve cannot be ruled out as a >50% breach even though its maximum is 30%.
Correct ranges and at-most-one-breaching-issuer bound; attributes HOOD's growth partly to a low base/non-recurring mix more strongly than selected facts show.

Correctly refuses a definite policy verdict; describes COIN's transaction-heavy revenue as sharply expanded though the selected packet proves total YoY growth and transaction QoQ decline, not transaction YoY growth.
